## How this work is cited

Passages inside A Vindication of the Rights of Woman are identified by chapter, or the introduction. The corpus has one entry cited without a chapter and the rest with one. The chapter is what identifies the passage, so the chapterless entry is the less complete record.

## The work in Mary Wollstonecraft’s thought

Mary Wollstonecraft (1759–1797) was an English radical writer whose A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792) founded modern liberal feminist argument. She wrote on education, the French Revolution, and travel, and mixed in Dissenting and Jacobin circles. [More on Mary Wollstonecraft](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mary-wollstonecraft) .
